title: Office — the questions before anything is drawn

steps.path: The editors inside the Office download
steps.headline: Which version of the OnlyOffice editors should Office be built on?
steps.today: The trial used the original OnlyOffice editors. A 2026 copy called Euro-Office has the same editors, made by Nextcloud and others after a dispute over OnlyOffice's logo rule.
steps.problem: The original's licence asks that its logo stay visible inside the editor. Euro-Office drops that rule, but it is newer and I have not tested it yet.
steps.proposal: Pick which to build on. Switching later is possible because the two are nearly identical, but it costs a re-test.

options.label: Test Euro-Office first
pros: A day's trial on your same six files tells us if it is as good before we commit.
If it passes, the editor can look fully like YouCoded, with no outside logo.
cons: Adds about a day before design starts.
If it fails, we are back to the original with a logo.

options.label: Original OnlyOffice
pros: Proven in the trial on your own files.
New features arrive here first.
cons: A small OnlyOffice logo stays in a corner of every open document.
The company has been hostile to projects that remove its logo.

options.label: Euro-Office, untested
pros: No logo rule, so the editor can be fully in YouCoded's style.
Backed by several European companies.
cons: Untested on your files.
May lag behind the original on new features.

steps.path: The first time you open Office
steps.headline: When should the Office editors be downloaded?
steps.today: Nothing is downloaded yet. The editors measured about 63 MB, plus fonts, and are too big to add to every YouCoded download.
steps.problem: Someone who never uses Office should not pay for it, but someone who does should not be surprised by a wait.

options.label: First time opened
pros: Only people who use Office download it.
Same pattern as downloading a local AI model today.
cons: The first open waits about a minute on a normal connection.
Needs internet that first time.

options.label: Quietly after install
pros: Ready the first time you want it.
cons: Uses data and disk for people who never open Office.
A surprise download some people will not like.

options.label: In the main installer
pros: Works offline from day one.
cons: Every YouCoded download grows by about 65–145 MB.
Office updates would need a full app update.

steps.headline: Which fonts should come with Office?
steps.today: The trial package carries 203 fonts, 81 MB of the download. Your computer also has its own fonts installed.
steps.problem: A document asking for a font we do not have shows a look-alike instead, which can shift line breaks and page counts.
steps.proposal: Choose how many fonts ship, and whether your own installed fonts are used too.

options.label: Core set + yours
options.summary: About 25 common look-alikes (for Calibri, Times, Arial and similar), plus every font already on your computer.
pros: Download stays near 80 MB instead of 145 MB.
Your own installed fonts just work.
cons: A rare font the document uses may show as a look-alike.
On phones there are fewer installed fonts to fall back on.

options.label: All 203 fonts
pros: Fewest look-alike swaps.
cons: Download near 145 MB.
Most of the fonts are for languages you may never use.

options.label: Fetch when needed
pros: Smallest first download.
A missing font appears once it arrives.
cons: A document can briefly show the wrong font, then jump.
Needs internet the first time each font is used.

steps.page: Where Office lives in the app
steps.intro: These decide how you get to Office and how open documents are arranged.

steps.path: The buttons at the top left of the app
steps.headline: How do you get to the Office page?
steps.today: The top left of the app holds the Pages button and up to four pinned pages.
steps.problem: Office is a big feature; if it is hard to find, it will not be used, but it also should not crowd out your own pages.

options.label: Its own button
options.summary: A built-in Office button at the top left, always present, separate from your pinned pages.
pros: Always one press away.
Does not use up one of your four pinned-page spots.
cons: One more button in the header for people who never use Office.
Needs a setting to hide it.

options.label: A pinnable page
pros: Behaves exactly like your other pages.
Only there if you pin it.
cons: Uses one of your four pinned spots.
New users will not find it unless told.

options.label: Only from files
pros: No new button at all.
cons: Cannot start a new blank document without a file first.
No home for recent documents or templates.

steps.path: The Office page, with several documents open
steps.headline: How should several open documents be arranged?
steps.today: Nothing exists yet. OnlyOffice on your computer shows each open document as a tab along the top of one window.
steps.problem: Each open document uses a few hundred megabytes of memory, so the arrangement also decides how heavy Office gets.

options.label: Tabs in one page
pros: Familiar from OnlyOffice and web browsers.
Easy to hop between a memo and its spreadsheet.
cons: Many tabs means much memory, unless idle tabs are put to sleep (asked below).

options.label: Separate windows
pros: Two documents side by side on a big screen.
cons: Windows to manage outside YouCoded.
Harder to do on phones.

options.label: One at a time
pros: Lightest on memory.
Simplest to understand.
cons: Switching documents closes the current one.

steps.path: Tabs you have not looked at for a while
steps.headline: Should documents you are not looking at be put to sleep to save memory?
steps.today: In the trial, a big spreadsheet used about 1 GB of memory, and a Word memo about half that.
steps.problem: Five open documents could use several gigabytes and slow the whole computer, especially a laptop.
steps.proposal: A tab idle for a while is saved to a recovery copy and closed in the background; returning to it reopens it in 1–3 seconds, at the same place. Yes builds this; No keeps every tab live.

steps.path: The Office page, with no document open
steps.headline: What should the Office start screen offer?
steps.today: Nothing exists yet. OnlyOffice's own start screen has New, Recent, Templates and Open.
steps.problem: This is the first thing you see; too little and it feels empty, too much and it feels like a second app.
steps.proposal: Pick every item that belongs on the start screen.

options.label: New blank files
options.summary: New document, spreadsheet and presentation buttons.
pros: The main reason to open Office without a file.
cons: None worth naming.

options.label: Recent documents
options.summary: The Office files you opened lately, from anywhere.
pros: One press back into yesterday's work.
cons: Shows file names to anyone looking at your screen.

options.label: Templates
options.summary: A starter memo, budget sheet, slide deck and similar.
pros: Faster start than a blank page.
cons: Someone has to choose and maintain them.

options.label: This project's files
options.summary: The Office files in the project you are working in.
pros: Ties Office to the project the assistant is working on.
cons: Repeats what the Project View already shows.

options.label: Ask the assistant
options.summary: A box: describe a document and the assistant drafts it, then opens it here.
pros: The thing only YouCoded's office can do.
cons: Needs the assistant working; more to design and build.

steps.intro: The session drawer and the Project View already preview Word, Excel and PDF files. These decide how editing works there.

steps.path: Opening a Word or Excel file from the session drawer or Project View
steps.headline: When you open an Office file in the file viewer, what should appear first?
steps.today: A quick preview appears instantly, but you cannot change anything; an Excel file is look-only.
steps.problem: The real editor takes 1–6 seconds to start, so opening straight into it makes every glance at a file slower.

options.label: Preview, then Edit
pros: Glancing at files stays instant.
Memory is only used when you actually edit.
cons: One extra press to start editing.
The preview and the editor can look slightly different.

options.label: Straight to editor
pros: What you see is exactly what you edit.
No extra press.
cons: Every file you open waits 1–6 seconds.
Browsing through several files uses much more memory.

steps.path: Editing a Word or Excel file inside the file viewer
steps.headline: What should the small editor in the file viewer look like?
steps.today: Nothing exists yet. The full OnlyOffice ribbon is several rows deep and wide.
steps.problem: The file viewer is a narrow panel; the full ribbon would not fit and would crowd out the document.

options.label: YouCoded's own bar
options.summary: One slim row drawn by YouCoded: font, bold, italic, lists, alignment, undo, and Open in Office.
pros: Looks exactly like the rest of the app in every theme.
Only the tools that fit a quick edit.
cons: Anything beyond the basics means pressing Open in Office.
More for us to build.

options.label: OnlyOffice compact bar
pros: More tools without leaving the viewer.
Less for us to build.
cons: Looks like OnlyOffice, not YouCoded.
Cramped in a narrow panel.

steps.path: Which files open in the Office editors
steps.headline: Which kinds of files should Office edit?
steps.today: The file viewer previews Word, Excel, CSV and PDF files. PowerPoint and OpenDocument files show only a file name.
steps.problem: Each kind added is more to test, and some kinds lose details when saved.
steps.proposal: Pick every kind the first version should edit.

options.label: Word, Excel, PowerPoint
options.summary: .docx, .xlsx and .pptx.
pros: The files people actually send you.
cons: None worth naming.

options.label: OpenDocument files
options.summary: .odt, .ods and .odp, from LibreOffice.
pros: Opens files from LibreOffice users.
cons: Some formatting may shift when saved back.

options.label: CSV tables
options.summary: Plain comma-separated tables, which the assistant often produces.
pros: Fixes today's look-only spreadsheet complaint for CSVs.
cons: Formatting you add cannot be saved in a CSV; it would need saving as Excel.

options.label: PDF notes and forms
options.summary: Highlight, comment and fill in forms. Not rewriting a PDF's text.
pros: Fill in a form without leaving the app.
cons: People may expect full PDF editing, which this is not.

options.label: Old .doc, .xls, .ppt
options.summary: Opens them; saving converts to the modern kind, after asking.
pros: Old files from older Office versions just open.
cons: Saving creates a new file with a different ending.

steps.intro: How your changes reach the file on disk, and how the assistant works inside a document.

steps.path: Saving a document you are editing
steps.headline: How should saving work?
steps.today: OnlyOffice on your computer saves when you press Save. Google Docs and Word online save every few seconds by themselves.
steps.problem: Saving by itself means a mistake reaches the real file at once; saving only on press means a crash can lose work.

options.label: Save + safety copy
options.summary: The real file changes only when you press Save; a hidden recovery copy is kept every few seconds.
pros: The original is never changed by accident.
A crash or closed app loses nothing; it offers to restore.
cons: You must remember to press Save; an unsaved dot shows on the tab.

options.label: Save automatically
pros: Never think about saving.
Matches Google Docs.
cons: Every change hits the real file right away, including mistakes.
A file another program has open could be overwritten.

options.label: Only when pressed
pros: Simplest; matches OnlyOffice on your computer.
cons: A crash loses everything since the last save.

steps.path: Asking the assistant to change the document you have open
steps.headline: When the assistant changes an open document, how should its changes appear?
steps.today: The assistant can already write files on disk, but it cannot touch a document open in an editor.
steps.problem: Changes that appear silently are fast but easy to miss; changes you must approve are safe but slow for many small edits.
steps.proposal: Two ways the assistant's edits could show up.

options.label: Straight in, undoable
options.summary: You watch the change happen; Undo takes it back like any edit.
pros: Fast, and you see it live.
Works the same in documents, spreadsheets and slides.
cons: A change in a part of the document you are not looking at is easy to miss.

options.label: As suggestions
options.summary: Word-style tracked changes you accept or reject one by one.
pros: Nothing changes without your yes.
A clear record of what the assistant did.
cons: Tedious for many small edits.
Spreadsheets and slides have no tracked-changes mode, so it only works for Word files.

steps.path: Chatting while a document is open
steps.headline: How much should the assistant know about the document you have open?
steps.today: The assistant only sees a file when you attach it or ask it to read one.
steps.problem: Having to attach the file you are looking at is a chore, but sending every open document's contents with every message is a privacy and cost worry.

options.label: Knows which, reads on ask
options.summary: It knows the file name and what you have selected; it reads the contents only when your message needs them.
pros: "Fix this paragraph" just works.
Contents are not sent with messages that have nothing to do with the document.
cons: The file's name and your selection are shared with every message.

options.label: Always reads it
pros: Always fully informed.
cons: Every message carries the whole document: slower and costlier, and privacy-heavy.

options.label: Only when attached
pros: Nothing is shared unless you choose.
cons: You must attach the document every time you ask about it.

steps.page: Look, phones and the first version
steps.intro: How far the theme goes, when phones get Office, and what the first testable version must do.

steps.path: The Office editor under your current theme
steps.headline: How far should your theme reach into the Office editor?
steps.today: The trial showed the editor taking on Midnight's colours, and Meadow Mist's wallpaper and glass. The page itself stays white paper.
steps.problem: Deeper theming looks better but is more that can break when OnlyOffice updates.

options.label: Colours, font, glass
pros: Office feels like part of YouCoded in every theme.
Wallpaper themes stay beautiful.
cons: More to re-check each time the editors update.

options.label: Colours only
pros: Matches the theme, with less that can break.
cons: Wallpaper themes show a solid block where the editor is.

options.label: OnlyOffice's own look
pros: Nothing to maintain.
cons: Looks like a different app dropped into YouCoded.

steps.path: Office on the Android app and the phone remote
steps.headline: When should phones get Office?
steps.today: The trial squeezed the desktop editor onto a phone screen: it worked, but page text was tiny and the toolbar cramped.
steps.problem: A proper phone layout exists in the package but needs its own wiring and theming, and phones have far less memory.

options.label: Desktop first
pros: The first version reaches you sooner.
Phone work learns from desktop mistakes.
cons: On phones, Office files stay preview-only for a while.

options.label: Both together
pros: Same features everywhere from day one.
cons: The first version takes noticeably longer.

steps.path: The first version you will test
steps.headline: What must work before you test the first version?
steps.today: You said nothing merges until the build reaches a point you can demo and test.
steps.problem: Waiting for everything delays your first real try by weeks; too little leaves nothing worth testing.
steps.proposal: Pick everything the first testable version must have. The rest follows after your first try.

options.label: Office page + tabs
options.summary: Download on first open, start screen, open, edit, save.
pros: The core of the whole feature.
cons: None worth naming.

options.label: Editing in file viewers
options.summary: Edit button in the session drawer and Project View, with Open in Office.
pros: Where most files the assistant makes are seen first.
cons: Adds about a week before your first try.

options.label: Theme matching
pros: You judge the real look, not OnlyOffice's default.
cons: Adds a few days.

options.label: Assistant editing
options.summary: The assistant changes the open document live.
pros: The part that makes it YouCoded's office.
cons: The largest single piece; adds one to two weeks.
